title: Afsharid Iran
capsule: The Afsharid dynasty was founded by Nader Shah, a Turkic Afshar chieftain from Khorasan who deposed the last Safavid shah and crowned himself king of Iran in 1736. At the peak of his power Nader Shah sacked Delhi in 1739, looting the Peacock Throne and the Koh-i-Noor diamond, extended Iranian authority into Central Asia and the Caucasus, and briefly seized Oman; his campaigns created the largest Iranian empire since the Sassanids. His assassination in 1747 triggered immediate fragmentation: his empire broke into competing Afsharid, Zand, and Durrani successor states, with the main Afsharid line maintaining control of Khorasan until displaced by the Qajars in 1796.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The empire's core in Iran and Khorasan is well attested; the peripheral territories in the Caucasus, Central Asia, and the Indian subcontinent were held briefly and their precise boundaries during the reign are poorly documented.
